def handle_generate_command(linter: PyLinter) -> int:
    """Handle 'pylint-config generate'."""
    # Interactively generate a pylint configuration
    if linter.config.interactive:
        generate_interactive_config(linter)
        return 0
    print(get_subparser_help(linter, "generate"))
    return 32

    ) -> int:

    def setUp(self):

        # Create a mock BadNames object with controlled return values
        self.mock_bad_names = Mock()
        self.mock_bad_names.get = Mock()

    def test_get_bad_names_with_class_node(self):
        """Test get_bad_names when node_name is 'class'."""
        # Setup mock to return specific value for 'klass'
        self.mock_bad_names.get.return_value = 5
        stats = LinterStats(bad_names=self.mock_bad_names)
        
        result = stats.get_bad_names("class")
        
        # Verify mock was called with correct parameters
        self.mock_bad_names.get.assert_called_once_with("klass", 0)
        self.assertEqual(result, 5)

    def test_get_bad_names_with_non_class_node(self):
        """Test get_bad_names when node_name is not 'class'."""
        # Setup mock to return specific value for 'function'
        self.mock_bad_names.get.return_value = 3
        stats = LinterStats(bad_names=self.mock_bad_names)
        
        result = stats.get_bad_names("function")
        
        # Verify mock was called with correct parameters
        self.mock_bad_names.get.assert_called_once_with("function", 0)
        self.assertEqual(result, 3)

    def test_get_bad_names_returns_zero_when_key_not_found(self):
        """Test get_bad_names returns 0 when key is not in bad_names."""
        # Setup mock to return 0 (default value)
        self.mock_bad_names.get.return_value = 0
        stats = LinterStats(bad_names=self.mock_bad_names)
        
        result = stats.get_bad_names("nonexistent")
        
        # Verify mock was called with correct parameters
        self.mock_bad_names.get.assert_called_once_with("nonexistent", 0)
        self.assertEqual(result, 0)

    def test_get_bad_names_with_all_valid_node_types(self):
        """Test get_bad_names with all possible valid node_name values."""
        test_cases = [
            "argument", "attr", "class", "class_attribute", "class_const",
            "const", "inlinevar", "function", "method", "module", "variable",
            "typevar", "paramspec", "typevartuple", "typealias"
        ]
        
        stats = LinterStats(bad_names=self.mock_bad_names)
        
        for node_name in test_cases:
            with self.subTest(node_name=node_name):
                # Reset mock for each test
                self.mock_bad_names.get.reset_mock()
                expected_key = "klass" if node_name == "class" else node_name
                expected_value = hash(node_name) % 10  # Some unique value
                self.mock_bad_names.get.return_value = expected_value
                
                result = stats.get_bad_names(node_name)
                
                self.mock_bad_names.get.assert_called_once_with(expected_key, 0)
                self.assertEqual(result, expected_value)

    def test_get_bad_names_with_default_bad_names(self):
        """Test get_bad_names when using default BadNames instance."""
        stats = LinterStats()
        
        # Test with 'class' node_name
        result = stats.get_bad_names("class")
        self.assertEqual(result, 0)  # Default BadNames should have 0 for 'klass'
        
        # Test with other node_name
        result = stats.get_bad_names("function")
        self.assertEqual(result, 0)  # Default BadNames should have 0 for 'function'

        # All valid node types from the Literal annotation
        valid_types = [

            "const", "inlinevar", "function", "method", "module", "variable",
            "typevar", "paramspec", "typevartuple", "typealias"
        ]
        
        for node_type in valid_types:
            with self.subTest(node_type=node_type):
                self.mock_bad_names.get.reset_mock()
                self.mock_bad_names.get.return_value = 1
                
                result = stats.get_bad_names(node_type)
                
                expected_key = "klass" if node_type == "class" else node_type
                self.mock_bad_names.get.assert_called_once_with(expected_key, 0)
                self.assertEqual(result, 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":

        """Update stats."""
        i = 0
        tokens = list(tokens)
        while i < len(tokens):

def on_set_current_module(self, module: str, filepath: str | None) -> None:
        """Set the format template to be used and check for unrecognized arguments."""
        template = str(self.linter.config.msg_template or self._template)

        # Return early if the template is the same as the previous one
        if template == self._template:
            return

        # Set template to the currently selected template
        self._template = template

        # Check to see if all parameters in the template are attributes of the Message
        arguments = re.findall(r"\{(\w+?)(:.*)?\}", template)
        for argument in arguments:
            if argument[0] not in MESSAGE_FIELDS:
                warnings.warn(
                    f"Don't recognize the argument '{argument[0]}' in the --msg-template. "
                    "Are you sure it is supported on the current version of pylint?",
                    stacklevel=2,
                )
                template = re.sub(r"\{" + argument[0] + r"(:.*?)?\}", "", template)
        self._fixed_template = template

def get_full_documentation(
        self,
        msgs: dict[str, MessageDefinitionTuple],
        options: Iterable[tuple[str, OptionDict, Any]],
        reports: Sequence[tuple[str, str, ReportsCallable]],
        doc: str | None = None,
        module: str | None = None,
        show_options: bool = True,
    ) -> str:
        result = ""
        checker_title = f"{self.name.replace('_', ' ').title()} checker"
        if module:
            # Provide anchor to link against
            result += f".. _{module}:\n\n"
        result += f"{get_rst_title(checker_title, '~')}\n"
        if module:
            result += f"This checker is provided by ``{module}``.\n"
        result += f"Verbatim name of the checker is ``{self.name}``.\n\n"
        if doc:
            # Provide anchor to link against
            result += get_rst_title(f"{checker_title} Documentation", "^")
            result += f"{cleandoc(doc)}\n\n"
        # options might be an empty generator and not be False when cast to boolean
        options_list = list(options)
        if options_list:
            if show_options:
                result += get_rst_title(f"{checker_title} Options", "^")
                result += f"{get_rst_section(None, options_list)}\n"
            else:
                result += f"See also :ref:`{self.name} checker's options' documentation <{self.name}-options>`\n\n"
        if msgs:
            result += get_rst_title(f"{checker_title} Messages", "^")
            for msgid, msg in sorted(
                msgs.items(), key=lambda kv: (_MSG_ORDER.index(kv[0][0]), kv[0])
            ):
                msg_def = self.create_message_definition_from_tuple(msgid, msg)
                result += f"{msg_def.format_help(checkerref=False)}\n"
            result += "\n"
        if reports:
            result += get_rst_title(f"{checker_title} Reports", "^")
            for report in reports:
                result += f":{report[0]}: {report[1]}\n"
            result += "\n"
        result += "\n"
        return result

def finalize(self) -> str:
        """Format and print messages in the context of the path."""
        messages: list[str] = []
        for msg in self.messages:
            obj = ""
            if msg.obj:
                obj = f":{msg.obj}"
            messages.append(f"{msg.msg_id[0]}:{msg.line:>3}{obj}: {msg.msg}")

        messages.sort()
        for message in messages:
            print(message, file=self.out)

        result = self.out.getvalue()
        self.reset()
        return result

def visit_functiondef(self, node: nodes.FunctionDef) -> None:
        """Check use of super."""
        # ignore actual functions or method within a new style class
        if not node.is_method():
            return
        klass = node.parent.frame()
        for stmt in node.nodes_of_class(nodes.Call):
            if node_frame_class(stmt) != node_frame_class(node):
                # Don't look down in other scopes.
                continue

            expr = stmt.func
            if not isinstance(expr, nodes.Attribute):
                continue

            match call := expr.expr:
                case nodes.Call(func=nodes.Name(name="super"), args=[arg0, *_]):
                    pass
                case _:
                    # skip the test if using super
                    # super first arg should not be the class
                    continue

            # calling super(type(self), self) can lead to recursion loop
            # in derived classes
            match arg0:
                case nodes.Call(func=nodes.Name(name="type")):
                    self.add_message("bad-super-call", node=call, args=("type",))
                    continue

            # calling super(self.__class__, self) can lead to recursion loop
            # in derived classes
            match call.args:
                case [
                    nodes.Attribute(attrname="__class__"),
                    nodes.Name(name="self"),
                    *_,
                ]:
                    self.add_message(
                        "bad-super-call", node=call, args=("self.__class__",)
                    )
                    continue

            try:
                supcls = call.args and next(call.args[0].infer(), None)
            except astroid.InferenceError:
                continue

            # If the supcls is in the ancestors of klass super can be used to skip
            # a step in the mro() and get a method from a higher parent
            if klass is not supcls and all(i != supcls for i in klass.ancestors()):
                name = None
                # if supcls is not Uninferable, then supcls was inferred
                # and use its name. Otherwise, try to look
                # for call.args[0].name
                if supcls:
                    name = supcls.name
                elif call.args and hasattr(call.args[0], "name"):
                    name = call.args[0].name
                if name:
                    self.add_message("bad-super-call", node=call, args=(name,))

def leave_functiondef(self, node: nodes.FunctionDef) -> None:
        # check left-over nested blocks stack
        self._emit_nested_blocks_message_if_needed(self._nested_blocks)
        # new scope = reinitialize the stack of nested blocks

def visit_yield(self, node: nodes.Yield) -> None:
        match node:
            case nodes.Yield(
                value=nodes.Name(name=name),
                parent=nodes.Expr(parent=nodes.For(body=[_]) as loop_node),
            ) if not isinstance(loop_node, nodes.AsyncFor):
                pass
            case _:
                # Avoid a false positive if the return value from `yield` is used,
                # (such as via Assign, AugAssign, etc).
                return

        if loop_node.target.name != name:
            return

        if isinstance(node.frame(), nodes.AsyncFunctionDef):
            return

        self.add_message("use-yield-from", node=loop_node, confidence=HIGH)

            self.position = len(self.content)
            return line + b'\n' if line else b''
        else:

f emit_node(
        self,
        name: str,
        type_: NodeType,
        properties: NodeProperties | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Create a new node.

        Nodes can be classes, packages, participants etc.
        """
        # pylint: disable=duplicate-code
        if properties is None:
            properties = NodeProperties(label=name)
        nodetype = self.NODES[type_]
        body = []
        if properties.attrs:
            # Escape attribute names to prevent Markdown formatting issues
            escaped_attrs = [
                self._escape_mermaid_text(attr) for attr in properties.attrs
            ]
            body.extend(escaped_attrs)
        if properties.methods:
            for func in properties.methods:
                args = self._get_method_arguments(func)
                # Escape method name and arguments
                escaped_method_name = self._escape_mermaid_text(func.name)
                escaped_args = [self._escape_mermaid_text(arg) for arg in args]
                line = f"{escaped_method_name}({', '.join(escaped_args)})"
                line += "*" if func.is_abstract() else ""
                if func.returns:
                    # Escape return type annotation
                    return_type = get_annotation_label(func.returns)
                    escaped_return_type = self._escape_mermaid_text(return_type)
                    line += f" {escaped_return_type}"
                body.append(line)
        name = name.split(".")[-1]
        self.emit(f"{nodetype} {name} {{")
        self._inc_indent()
        for line in body:
            self.emit(line)
        self._dec_indent()
        self.emit("}")
        # apply style for colored output
        if properties.color and properties.color != self.DEFAULT_COLOR:
            self.emit(f"style {name} fill:{properties.color}")

def prepare_crash_report(ex: Exception, filepath: str, crash_file_path: str) -> Path:
    issue_template_path = (
        Path(PYLINT_HOME) / datetime.now().strftime(str(crash_file_path))
    ).resolve()
    with open(filepath, encoding="utf8") as f:
        file_content = f.read()
    template = ""
    if not issue_template_path.exists():
        template = """\
First, please verify that the bug is not already filled:
https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/issues/

Then create a new issue:
https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/issues/new?labels=Crash 💥%2CNeeds triage 📥


"""
    template += f"""
Issue title:
Crash ``{ex}`` (if possible, be more specific about what made pylint crash)

### Bug description

When parsing the following ``a.py``:

<!--
 If sharing the code is not an option, please state so,
 but providing only the stacktrace would still be helpful.
 -->

```python
{file_content}
```

### Command used

```shell
pylint a.py
```

### Pylint output

<details open>
    <summary>
        pylint crashed with a ``{ex.__class__.__name__}`` and with the following stacktrace:
    </summary>

```python
"""
    template += traceback.format_exc()
    template += f"""
```


</details>

### Expected behavior

No crash.

### Pylint version

```shell
{full_version}
```

### OS / Environment

{sys.platform} ({platform.system()})

### Additional dependencies

<!--
Please remove this part if you're not using any of
your dependencies in the example.
 -->
"""
    try:
        with open(issue_template_path, "a", encoding="utf8") as f:
            f.write(template)
    except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
        print(
            f"Can't write the issue template for the crash in {issue_template_path} "
            f"because of: '{exc}'\nHere's the content anyway:\n{template}.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    return issue_template_path

def get_help(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> str:
    """Get the help message for the main 'pylint-config' command.

    Taken from argparse.ArgumentParser.format_help.
    """
    formatter = parser._get_formatter()

    # usage
    formatter.add_usage(
        parser.usage, parser._actions, parser._mutually_exclusive_groups
    )

    # description
    formatter.add_text(parser.description)

    # positionals, optionals and user-defined groups
    for action_group in parser._action_groups:
        if action_group.title == "Subcommands":
            formatter.start_section(action_group.title)
            formatter.add_text(action_group.description)
            formatter.add_arguments(action_group._group_actions)
            formatter.end_section()

    # epilog
    formatter.add_text(parser.epilog)

    # determine help from format above
    return formatter.format_help()

def get_subparser_help(linter: PyLinter, command: str) -> str:
    """Get the help message for one of the subcommands."""
    # Make sure subparsers are initialized properly
    assert linter._arg_parser._subparsers
    subparser_action = linter._arg_parser._subparsers._group_actions[0]
    assert isinstance(subparser_action, argparse._SubParsersAction)

    for name, subparser in subparser_action.choices.items():
        assert isinstance(subparser, argparse.ArgumentParser)
        if name == command:
            # Remove last character which is an extra new line
            return subparser.format_help()[:-1]
    return ""  # pragma: no cover

def same_root_dir(
        node: nodes.Import | nodes.ImportFrom, import_mod_name: str
    ) -> bool:
        """Does the node's file's path contain the base name of `import_mod_name`?"""
        if not import_mod_name:  # from . import ...
            return True
        if node.level:  # from .foo import ..., from ..bar import ...
            return True

        base_import_package = import_mod_name.split(".")[0]

        return base_import_package in Path(node.root().file).parent.parts

def load_results(
    base: str | Path, pylint_home: str | Path = PYLINT_HOME
) -> LinterStats | None:
    base = Path(base)
    pylint_home = Path(pylint_home)
    data_file = _get_pdata_path(base, 1, pylint_home)

    if not data_file.exists():
        return None

    try:
        with open(data_file, "rb") as stream:
            data = pickle.load(stream)
            if not isinstance(data, LinterStats):
                warnings.warn(
                    "You're using an old pylint cache with invalid data following "
                    f"an upgrade, please delete '{data_file}'.",
                    UserWarning,
                    stacklevel=2,
                )
                raise TypeError
            return data
    except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
        # There's an issue with the cache but we just continue as if it isn't there
        return None

from pylint.lint.caching import load_results, _get_pdata_path


# Create a mock LinterStats class for testing since we can't import the real one
class MockLinterStats:
    def __init__(self):
        self.module = "test_module"
        self.bad_names = 2


class TestLoadResults(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.base_path = Path(self.temp_dir) / "test_file.py"
        self.pylint_home = Path(self.temp_dir) / ".pylint"
        self.pylint_home.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        
        self.test_stats = MockLinterStats()

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir)

    def test_load_results_success(self):
        """Test successful loading of cached results."""
        with patch('pylint.lint.caching._get_pdata_path') as mock_get_path:
            mock_data_file = self.pylint_home / "test_cache.pkl"
            mock_get_path.return_value = mock_data_file
            
            with open(mock_data_file, "wb") as f:
                pickle.dump(self.test_stats, f)
            
            # Mock the LinterStats check in the actual function
            with patch('pylint.lint.caching.LinterStats', MockLinterStats):
                result = load_results(self.base_path, self.pylint_home)
            
            self.assertIsInstance(result, MockLinterStats)
            self.assertEqual(result.module, self.test_stats.module)
            self.assertEqual(result.bad_names, self.test_stats.bad_names)
            mock_get_path.assert_called_once_with(self.base_path, 1, self.pylint_home)

    def test_load_results_file_not_exists(self):
        """Test when cache file does not exist."""
        with patch('pylint.lint.caching._get_pdata_path') as mock_get_path:
            mock_data_file = self.pylint_home / "non_existent.pkl"
            mock_get_path.return_value = mock_data_file
            
            result = load_results(self.base_path, self.pylint_home)
            
            self.assertIsNone(result)
            mock_get_path.assert_called_once_with(self.base_path, 1, self.pylint_home)

    def test_load_results_invalid_data_type(self):
        """Test loading cache with invalid data type (old cache format)."""
        with patch('pylint.lint.caching._get_pdata_path') as mock_get_path:
            mock_data_file = self.pylint_home / "old_cache.pkl"
            mock_get_path.return_value = mock_data_file
            
            invalid_data = {"old": "data"}
            with open(mock_data_file, "wb") as f:
                pickle.dump(invalid_data, f)
            
            # Mock LinterStats for type checking
            with patch('pylint.lint.caching.LinterStats', MockLinterStats):
                with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
                    warnings.simplefilter("always")
                    result = load_results(self.base_path, self.pylint_home)
                    
                    self.assertIsNone(result)
                    self.assertEqual(len(w), 1)
                    self.assertIn("old pylint cache", str(w[0].message))
                    mock_get_path.assert_called_once_with(self.base_path, 1, self.pylint_home)

    def test_load_results_corrupted_pickle(self):
        """Test handling of corrupted pickle file."""
        with patch('pylint.lint.caching._get_pdata_path') as mock_get_path:
            mock_data_file = self.pylint_home / "corrupted.pkl"
            mock_get_path.return_value = mock_data_file
            
            with open(mock_data_file, "wb") as f:
                f.write(b"corrupted data")
            
            result = load_results(self.base_path, self.pylint_home)
            
            self.assertIsNone(result)
            mock_get_path.assert_called_once_with(self.base_path, 1, self.pylint_home)

        with patch('pylint.lint.caching._get_pdata_path') as mock_get_path:
            mock_data_file = self.pylint_home / "no_permission.pkl"
            mock_get_path.return_value = mock_data_file
            
            # Create a mock Path object that exists() returns True
            mock_path = MagicMock(spec=Path)
            mock_path.exists.return_value = True
            mock_get_path.return_value = mock_path
            
            with patch('builtins.open', side_effect=PermissionError("Access denied")):
                result = load_results(self.base_path, self.pylint_home)
                
                self.assertIsNone(result)
                mock_get_path.assert_called_once_with(self.base_path, 1, self.pylint_home)

        with patch('pylint.lint.caching._get_pdata_path') as mock_get_path:

            mock_get_path.return_value = mock_data_file

            original_pylint_home = PYLINT_HOME
            
            try:

                import pylint.lint.caching as caching_module

                with patch('pylint.lint.caching.LinterStats', MockLinterStats):

                caching_module.PYLINT_HOME = original_pylint_home

        """Test handling of IOError when reading file."""
        with patch('pylint.lint.caching._get_pdata_path') as mock_get_path:

            mock_data_file = MagicMock(spec=Path)

    def test_load_results_pickle_error(self):

def visit_importfrom(self, node: nodes.ImportFrom) -> None:
        if utils.in_type_checking_block(node):
            return
        # Only check imported names if the module is external
        if self.same_root_dir(node, node.modname):
            return

        names = [n[0] for n in node.names]

        # Check the imported objects first. If they are all valid type annotations,
        # the package can be private
        private_names = self._get_type_annotation_names(node, names)
        if not private_names:
            return

        # There are invalid imported objects, so check the name of the package
        private_module_imports = self._get_private_imports([node.modname])
        private_module_imports = self._get_type_annotation_names(
            node, private_module_imports
        )
        if private_module_imports:
            self.add_message(
                "import-private-name",
                node=node,
                args=("module", private_module_imports[0]),
                confidence=HIGH,
            )
            return  # Do not emit messages on the objects if the package is private

        private_names = self._get_private_imports(private_names)

        if private_names:
            imported_identifier = "objects" if len(private_names) > 1 else "object"
            private_name_string = ", ".join(private_names)
            self.add_message(
                "import-private-name",
                node=node,
                args=(imported_identifier, private_name_string),
                confidence=HIGH,
            )

        """Create a diagram object."""

        ent = PackageEntity(title, node)

def format(
        self,
        layout: BaseLayout,
        stream: TextIO = sys.stdout,
        encoding: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Format and write the given layout into the stream object.

        unicode policy: unicode strings may be found in the layout;
        try to call 'stream.write' with it, but give it back encoded using
        the given encoding if it fails
        """
        if not encoding:
            encoding = getattr(stream, "encoding", "UTF-8")
        self.encoding = encoding or "UTF-8"
        self.out = stream
        self.begin_format()
        layout.accept(self)
        self.end_format()

def get_table_content(self, table: Table) -> list[list[str]]:
        """Trick to get table content without actually writing it.

        return an aligned list of lists containing table cells values as string
        """
        result: list[list[str]] = [[]]
        cols = table.cols
        for cell in self.compute_content(table):
            if cols == 0:
                result.append([])
                cols = table.cols
            cols -= 1
            result[-1].append(cell)
        # fill missing cells
        result[-1] += [""] * (cols - len(result[-1]))
        return result

def compute_content(self, layout: BaseLayout) -> Iterator[str]:
        """Trick to compute the formatting of children layout before actually
        writing it.

        return an iterator on strings (one for each child element)
        """
        # Patch the underlying output stream with a fresh-generated stream,
        # which is used to store a temporary representation of a child
        # node.
        out = self.out
        try:
            for child in layout.children:
                stream = StringIO()
                self.out = stream
                child.accept(self)
                yield stream.getvalue()
        finally:
            self.out = out

def enable(
        self,
        msgid: str,
        scope: str = "package",
        line: int | None = None,
        ignore_unknown: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Enable a message for a scope."""
        self._set_msg_status(
            msgid, enable=True, scope=scope, line=line, ignore_unknown=ignore_unknown
        )
        self._register_by_id_managed_msg(msgid, line, is_disabled=False)

def is_message_enabled(
        self,
        msg_descr: str,
        line: int | None = None,
        confidence: interfaces.Confidence | None = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Is this message enabled for the current file ?

        Optionally, is it enabled for this line and confidence level ?

        The current file is implicit and mandatory. As a result this function
        can't be cached right now as the line is the line of the currently
        analysed file (self.file_state), if it changes, then the result for
        the same msg_descr/line might need to change.

        :param msg_descr: Either the msgid or the symbol for a MessageDefinition
        :param line: The line of the currently analysed file
        :param confidence: The confidence of the message
        """
        if confidence and confidence.name not in self.linter.config.confidence:
            return False
        try:
            msgids = self.linter.msgs_store.message_id_store.get_active_msgids(
                msg_descr
            )
        except exceptions.UnknownMessageError:
            # The linter checks for messages that are not registered
            # due to version mismatch, just treat them as message IDs
            # for now.
            msgids = [msg_descr]
        return any(self._is_one_message_enabled(msgid, line) for msgid in msgids)

def mark_as_consumed(self, name: str, consumed_nodes: list[nodes.NodeNG]) -> None:
        """Mark the given nodes as consumed for the name.

        If all of the nodes for the name were consumed, delete the name from
        the to_consume dictionary
        """
        unconsumed = [n for n in self.to_consume[name] if n not in set(consumed_nodes)]
        self.consumed[name] = consumed_nodes

        if unconsumed:
            self.to_consume[name] = unconsumed
        else:
            del self.to_consume[name]

def __init__(self, node: nodes.NodeNG, scope_type: str):
        self.node = node
        self.scope_type = scope_type

        self.to_consume = copy.copy(node.locals)
        self.consumed = {}
        self.consumed_uncertain = defaultdict(list)

        self.names_under_always_false_test: set[str] = set()

    get_functional_test_files_from_directory,
)


class TestGetFunctionalTestFilesFromDirectory(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test get_functional_test_files_from_directory function."""

    def setUp(self):
        """Set up a temporary directory for testing."""
        self.temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.base_path = Path(self.temp_dir)

    def tearDown(self):
        """Clean up temporary directory."""
        import shutil

        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir)

    def create_test_structure(self, structure):
        """Helper to create directory/file structure for testing.
        
        Args:
            structure: Dict mapping paths to either 'dir' or list of filenames
        """
        for path, value in structure.items():
            full_path = self.base_path / path
            if value == "dir":
                full_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            elif isinstance(value, list):
                full_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                for filename in value:
                    (full_path.parent / filename).touch()

    def test_empty_directory(self):
        """Test with an empty directory."""
        # Mock the _check_functional_tests_structure to avoid validation errors
        with mock.patch(
            "pylint.testutils.functional.find_functional_tests._check_functional_tests_structure"
        ) as mock_check:
            result = get_functional_test_files_from_directory(self.temp_dir)
            mock_check.assert_called_once()
            self.assertEqual(result, [])

    def test_single_python_file(self):
        """Test with a single Python file."""
        # Create proper structure: file in directory named after first letters of filename
        test_dir = self.base_path / "te"
        test_dir.mkdir()
        test_file = test_dir / "test_file.py"
        test_file.touch()
        
        result = get_functional_test_files_from_directory(self.temp_dir)
        
        self.assertEqual(len(result), 1)
        self.assertIsInstance(result[0], FunctionalTestFile)
        # Check the file path using the FunctionalTestFile's __repr__ or other attributes
        self.assertEqual(str(result[0]), str(test_file))

    def test_ignore_init_py(self):
        """Test that __init__.py files are ignored."""
        # Create proper structure
        test_dir = self.base_path / "te"
        test_dir.mkdir()
        init_file = test_dir / "__init__.py"
        test_file = test_dir / "test.py"
        init_file.touch()
        test_file.touch()
        
        result = get_functional_test_files_from_directory(self.temp_dir)
        
        self.assertEqual(len(result), 1)
        # Check that the result contains the test.py file, not __init__.py

"""Unit tests for the visit_global method of VariablesChecker."""

import unittest
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
import astroid
from pylint.checkers.variables import VariablesChecker
from pylint.testutils import MessageTest
from pylint.testutils.checker_test_case import CheckerTestCase


class TestVisitGlobal(CheckerTestCase):
    """Test cases for VariablesChecker.visit_global."""

    CHECKER_CLASS = VariablesChecker

    def setUp(self):
        """Set up test fixtures."""
        super().setUp()
        self.checker = self.CHECKER_CLASS(linter=self.linter)

    def test_global_at_module_level(self):
        """Test global statement at module level raises appropriate message."""
        # Create a mock Global node with module frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["test_var"]
        
        # Mock frame to be a Module
        module_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.Module)
        node.frame.return_value = module_frame
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        with self.assertAddsMessages(
            MessageTest(msg_id="global-at-module-level", node=node, confidence=3)
        ):
            self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_global_variable_not_assigned(self):
        """Test global variable not assigned locally raises appropriate message."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["unassigned_var"]
        node.lineno = 1
        node.col_offset = 0
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef (not module)
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.side_effect = astroid.NotFoundError
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock utils functions to return False
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=False):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=False):
                with self.assertAddsMessages(
                    MessageTest(
                        msg_id="global-variable-not-assigned",
                        args="unassigned_var",
                        node=node,
                        confidence=3,
                    )
                ):
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_redefined_builtin(self):
        """Test global redefined builtin raises appropriate message."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["list"]
        node.lineno = 1
        node.col_offset = 0
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create a mock AssignName node
        assign_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node.name = "list"
        assign_node.frame.return_value = MagicMock()
        
        # Mock root() to return a module with special_attributes
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.return_value = [assign_node]
        module_root.special_attributes = ["list"]
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock utils functions to return True (so we don't get other messages)
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=True):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=True):
                with self.assertAddsMessages(
                    MessageTest(msg_id="redefined-builtin", args="list", node=node)
                ):
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_global_variable_undefined(self):
        """Test global variable undefined at module scope raises appropriate message."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["undefined_var"]
        node.lineno = 1
        node.col_offset = 0
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create a mock AssignName node that's not at module level
        assign_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node.frame.return_value = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.return_value = [assign_node]
        module_root.special_attributes = []
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock utils functions to return False
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=False):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=False):
                with self.assertAddsMessages(
                    MessageTest(
                        msg_id="global-variable-undefined",
                        args="undefined_var",
                        node=node,
                        confidence=3,
                    )
                ):
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_valid_global_statement(self):
        """Test valid global statement raises default message."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["valid_var"]
        node.lineno = 1
        node.col_offset = 0
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create a mock AssignName node at module level
        assign_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node.frame.return_value = node.root.return_value
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.return_value = [assign_node]
        module_root.special_attributes = []
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock utils functions to return True
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=True):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=True):
                with self.assertAddsMessages(
                    MessageTest(msg_id="global-statement", node=node, confidence=3)
                ):
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_module_level_function_assignment(self):
        """Test global referencing module-level function does not raise undefined error."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["module_func"]
        node.lineno = 1
        node.col_offset = 0
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create a mock FunctionDef node at module level
        func_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        func_node.frame.return_value = node.root.return_value
        func_node.parent = node.root.return_value
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.return_value = [func_node]
        module_root.special_attributes = []
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock utils functions to return False
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=False):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=False):
                # Should not raise any messages since it's a module-level function
                with self.assertNoMessages():
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_locally_defined_by_import(self):
        """Test global variable locally defined by import does not raise messages."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["imported_var"]
        node.lineno = 1
        node.col_offset = 0
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.side_effect = astroid.NotFoundError
        # The variable is defined locally by import
        import_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.Import)
        module_root.locals = {"imported_var": [import_node]}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock utils functions to return False
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=False):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=False):
                # Should not raise any messages since it's defined locally by import
                with self.assertNoMessages():
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_multiple_names_with_different_conditions(self):
        """Test global statement with multiple names with different conditions."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["valid_var", "undefined_var", "list"]
        node.lineno = 1
        node.col_offset = 0
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create mock assign nodes for different names
        assign_node_valid = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node_valid.frame.return_value = node.root.return_value
        
        assign_node_undefined = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node_undefined.frame.return_value = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        
        assign_node_builtin = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node_builtin.name = "list"
        assign_node_builtin.frame.return_value = node.root.return_value
        
        # Mock root() to return a module with different responses for different names
        def getattr_side_effect(name):
            if name == "valid_var":
                return [assign_node_valid]
            elif name == "undefined_var":
                return [assign_node_undefined]
            elif name == "list":
                return [assign_node_builtin]
            return []
        
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.side_effect = getattr_side_effect
        module_root.special_attributes = ["list"]
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock utils functions to return different values for different names
        def is_reassigned_side_effect(node, name):
            return name == "valid_var"
        
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  side_effect=is_reassigned_side_effect):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=False):
                with self.assertAddsMessages(
                    MessageTest(msg_id="global-statement", node=node, confidence=3),
                    MessageTest(
                        msg_id="global-variable-undefined",
                        args="undefined_var",
                        node=node,
                        confidence=3,
                    ),
                    MessageTest(
                        msg_id="redefined-builtin",
                        args="list",
                        node=node,
                    ),
                ):
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_class_def_module_level(self):
        """Test global referencing module-level class definition."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["ModuleClass"]
        node.lineno = 1
        node.col_offset = 0
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create a mock ClassDef node at module level
        class_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.ClassDef)
        class_node.frame.return_value = node.root.return_value
        class_node.parent = node.root.return_value
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.return_value = [class_node]
        module_root.special_attributes = []
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock utils functions to return False
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=False):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=False):
                # Should not raise any messages since it's a module-level class
                with self.assertNoMessages():
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Unit tests for the visit_global method of VariablesChecker."""

import unittest
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
import astroid
from pylint.checkers.variables import VariablesChecker
from pylint.testutils import MessageTest
from pylint.testutils.checker_test_case import CheckerTestCase
from pylint.interfaces import HIGH


class TestVisitGlobal(CheckerTestCase):
    """Test cases for VariablesChecker.visit_global."""

    CHECKER_CLASS = VariablesChecker

    def setUp(self):
        """Set up test fixtures."""
        super().setUp()
        self.checker = self.CHECKER_CLASS(linter=self.linter)

    def test_global_at_module_level(self):
        """Test global statement at module level raises appropriate message."""
        # Create a mock Global node with module frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["test_var"]
        
        # Mock frame to be a Module
        module_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.Module)
        node.frame.return_value = module_frame
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock position attributes
        position = MagicMock()
        position.lineno = 1
        position.col_offset = 0
        position.end_lineno = 1
        position.end_col_offset = 10
        node.position = position
        
        with self.assertAddsMessages(
            MessageTest(msg_id="global-at-module-level", node=node, confidence=HIGH)
        ):
            self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_global_variable_not_assigned(self):
        """Test global variable not assigned locally raises appropriate message."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["unassigned_var"]
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef (not module)
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.side_effect = astroid.NotFoundError
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock position attributes
        position = MagicMock()
        position.lineno = 1
        position.col_offset = 0
        position.end_lineno = 1
        position.end_col_offset = 15
        node.position = position
        
        # Mock utils functions to return False
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=False):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=False):
                with self.assertAddsMessages(
                    MessageTest(
                        msg_id="global-variable-not-assigned",
                        args="unassigned_var",
                        node=node,
                        confidence=HIGH,
                    )
                ):
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_redefined_builtin(self):
        """Test global redefined builtin raises appropriate message."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["list"]
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create a mock AssignName node
        assign_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node.name = "list"
        assign_node.frame.return_value = MagicMock()
        
        # Mock root() to return a module with special_attributes
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.return_value = [assign_node]
        module_root.special_attributes = ["list"]
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock position attributes
        position = MagicMock()
        position.lineno = 1
        position.col_offset = 0
        position.end_lineno = 1
        position.end_col_offset = 4
        node.position = position
        
        # Mock utils functions to return True (so we don't get other messages)
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=True):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=True):
                with self.assertAddsMessages(
                    MessageTest(msg_id="redefined-builtin", args="list", node=node)
                ):
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_global_variable_undefined(self):
        """Test global variable undefined at module scope raises appropriate message."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["undefined_var"]
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create a mock AssignName node that's not at module level
        assign_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node.frame.return_value = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.return_value = [assign_node]
        module_root.special_attributes = []
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock position attributes
        position = MagicMock()
        position.lineno = 1
        position.col_offset = 0
        position.end_lineno = 1
        position.end_col_offset = 13
        node.position = position
        
        # Mock utils functions to return False
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=False):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=False):
                with self.assertAddsMessages(
                    MessageTest(
                        msg_id="global-variable-undefined",
                        args="undefined_var",
                        node=node,
                        confidence=HIGH,
                    )
                ):
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_valid_global_statement(self):
        """Test valid global statement raises default message."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["valid_var"]
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create a mock AssignName node at module level
        assign_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node.frame.return_value = node.root.return_value
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.return_value = [assign_node]
        module_root.special_attributes = []
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock position attributes
        position = MagicMock()
        position.lineno = 1
        position.col_offset = 0
        position.end_lineno = 1
        position.end_col_offset = 9
        node.position = position
        
        # Mock utils functions to return True
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=True):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=True):
                with self.assertAddsMessages(
                    MessageTest(msg_id="global-statement", node=node, confidence=HIGH)
                ):
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_module_level_function_assignment(self):
        """Test global referencing module-level function does not raise undefined error."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["module_func"]
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create a mock FunctionDef node at module level
        func_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        func_node.frame.return_value = node.root.return_value
        func_node.parent = node.root.return_value
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.return_value = [func_node]
        module_root.special_attributes = []
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock position attributes
        position = MagicMock()
        position.lineno = 1
        position.col_offset = 0
        position.end_lineno = 1
        position.end_col_offset = 11
        node.position = position
        
        # Mock utils functions to return True (variable is reassigned or deleted)
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=True):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=True):
                # Should not raise any messages since it's a module-level function
                with self.assertNoMessages():
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_locally_defined_by_import(self):
        """Test global variable locally defined by import does not raise messages."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["imported_var"]
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.side_effect = astroid.NotFoundError
        # The variable is defined locally by import
        import_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.Import)
        module_root.locals = {"imported_var": [import_node]}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock position attributes
        position = MagicMock()
        position.lineno = 1
        position.col_offset = 0
        position.end_lineno = 1
        position.end_col_offset = 12
        node.position = position
        
        # Mock utils functions to return True (variable is reassigned or deleted)
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=True):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=True):
                # Should not raise any messages since it's defined locally by import
                with self.assertNoMessages():
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_multiple_names_with_different_conditions(self):
        """Test global statement with multiple names with different conditions."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["valid_var", "undefined_var", "list"]
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create mock assign nodes for different names
        assign_node_valid = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node_valid.frame.return_value = node.root.return_value
        
        assign_node_undefined = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node_undefined.frame.return_value = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        
        assign_node_builtin = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.AssignName)
        assign_node_builtin.name = "list"
        assign_node_builtin.frame.return_value = node.root.return_value
        
        # Mock root() to return a module with different responses for different names
        def getattr_side_effect(name):
            if name == "valid_var":
                return [assign_node_valid]
            elif name == "undefined_var":
                return [assign_node_undefined]
            elif name == "list":
                return [assign_node_builtin]
            return []
        
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.side_effect = getattr_side_effect
        module_root.special_attributes = ["list"]
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock position attributes
        position = MagicMock()
        position.lineno = 1
        position.col_offset = 0
        position.end_lineno = 1
        position.end_col_offset = 30
        node.position = position
        
        # Mock utils functions to return different values for different names
        def is_reassigned_side_effect(node, name):
            return name == "valid_var"
        
        def is_deleted_side_effect(node, name):
            return False
        
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  side_effect=is_reassigned_side_effect):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      side_effect=is_deleted_side_effect):
                with self.assertAddsMessages(
                    MessageTest(msg_id="global-statement", node=node, confidence=HIGH),
                    MessageTest(
                        msg_id="global-variable-undefined",
                        args="undefined_var",
                        node=node,
                        confidence=HIGH,
                    ),
                    MessageTest(
                        msg_id="redefined-builtin",
                        args="list",
                        node=node,
                    ),
                ):
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)

    def test_class_def_module_level(self):
        """Test global referencing module-level class definition."""
        # Create a mock Global node with function frame
        node = MagicMock()
        node.names = ["ModuleClass"]
        
        # Mock frame to be a FunctionDef
        function_frame = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.FunctionDef)
        node.frame.return_value = function_frame
        
        # Create a mock ClassDef node at module level
        class_node = MagicMock(spec=astroid.nodes.ClassDef)
        class_node.frame.return_value = node.root.return_value
        class_node.parent = node.root.return_value
        
        # Mock root() to return a module
        module_root = MagicMock()
        module_root.getattr.return_value = [class_node]
        module_root.special_attributes = []
        module_root.locals = {}
        node.root.return_value = module_root
        
        # Mock position attributes
        position = MagicMock()
        position.lineno = 1
        position.col_offset = 0
        position.end_lineno = 1
        position.end_col_offset = 11
        node.position = position
        
        # Mock utils functions to return True (variable is reassigned or deleted)
        with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_reassigned_after_current', 
                  return_value=True):
            with patch('pylint.checkers.variables.utils.is_deleted_after_current', 
                      return_value=True):
                # Should not raise any messages since it's a module-level class
                with self.assertNoMessages():
                    self.checker.visit_global(node)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def lazy_clone(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover
        """Concatenates the target directory and clones the file.

        Not expected to be tested as the primer won't work if it doesn't.
        It's tested in the continuous integration primers, only the coverage
        is not calculated on everything. If lazy clone breaks for local use
        we'll probably notice because we'll have a fatal when launching the
        primer locally.
        """
        logging.info("Lazy cloning %s", self.url)
        if not self.clone_directory.exists():
            return self._clone_repository()
        return self._pull_repository()

import unittest
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
import os
from io import StringIO

# Import the actual classes
from pylint.reporters.multi_reporter import MultiReporter
from pylint.reporters.base_reporter import BaseReporter
from pylint.lint import PyLinter


class TestMultiReporterLinter(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test cases for MultiReporter.linter method."""

    def setUp(self):
        """Set up test fixtures."""
        self.mock_close_output_files = Mock()
        self.mock_output = StringIO()
        
        # Create mock sub-reporters that properly implement the BaseReporter interface
        # We need to mock the linter property setter
        self.mock_sub_reporter1 = Mock(spec=BaseReporter)
        self.mock_sub_reporter2 = Mock(spec=BaseReporter)
        self.mock_sub_reporters = [self.mock_sub_reporter1, self.mock_sub_reporter2]
        
        # Create MultiReporter instance
        self.reporter = MultiReporter(
            sub_reporters=self.mock_sub_reporters,
            close_output_files=self.mock_close_output_files,
            output=self.mock_output
        )

    def test_linter_sets_internal_linter(self):
        """Test that linter method sets _linter attribute."""
        # Arrange
        mock_linter = Mock(spec=PyLinter)
        
        # Act
        self.reporter.linter(mock_linter)
        
        # Assert
        self.assertEqual(self.reporter._linter, mock_linter)

    def test_linter_sets_linter_on_all_sub_reporters(self):
        """Test that linter method sets linter on all sub-reporters."""
        # Arrange
        mock_linter = Mock(spec=PyLinter)
        
        # Act
        self.reporter.linter(mock_linter)
        
        # Assert
        # Check that linter was set on each sub-reporter
        for reporter in self.mock_sub_reporters:
            self.assertEqual(reporter.linter, mock_linter)

    def test_linter_with_empty_sub_reporters(self):
        """Test linter method with empty sub-reporters list."""
        # Arrange
        mock_linter = Mock(spec=PyLinter)
        reporter = MultiReporter(
            sub_reporters=[],
            close_output_files=self.mock_close_output_files,
            output=self.mock_output
        )
        
        # Act
        reporter.linter(mock_linter)
        
        # Assert
        self.assertEqual(reporter._linter, mock_linter)

    def test_linter_with_none_linter(self):
        """Test linter method with None value."""
        # Arrange
        mock_linter = None
        
        # Act
        self.reporter.linter(mock_linter)
        
        # Assert
        self.assertIsNone(self.reporter._linter)
        for reporter in self.mock_sub_reporters:
            self.assertEqual(reporter.linter, mock_linter)

    def test_linter_preserves_other_attributes(self):
        """Test that linter method doesn't affect other attributes."""
        # Arrange
        mock_linter = Mock(spec=PyLinter)
        original_messages = self.reporter.messages
        original_path_strip_prefix = self.reporter._path_strip_prefix
        
        # Act
        self.reporter.linter(mock_linter)
        
        # Assert
        self.assertEqual(self.reporter.messages, original_messages)
        self.assertEqual(self.reporter._path_strip_prefix, original_path_strip_prefix)
        self.assertEqual(self.reporter.close_output_files, self.mock_close_output_files)
        self.assertEqual(self.reporter.out, self.mock_output)

    def test_linter_chaining(self):
        """Test multiple calls to linter method."""
        # Arrange
        mock_linter1 = Mock(spec=PyLinter)
        mock_linter2 = Mock(spec=PyLinter)
        
        # Act - First call
        self.reporter.linter(mock_linter1)
        
        # Assert - First call
        self.assertEqual(self.reporter._linter, mock_linter1)
        for reporter in self.mock_sub_reporters:
            self.assertEqual(reporter.linter, mock_linter1)
        
        # Act - Second call
        self.reporter.linter(mock_linter2)
        
        # Assert - Second call
        self.assertEqual(self.reporter._linter, mock_linter2)
        for reporter in self.mock_sub_reporters:
            self.assertEqual(reporter.linter, mock_linter2)

    def test_linter_with_different_sub_reporter_types(self):
        """Test linter method with sub-reporters that have different implementations."""
        # Arrange
        mock_linter = Mock(spec=PyLinter)
        
        # Create mock reporters
        mock_reporter1 = Mock()
        mock_reporter2 = Mock()
        
        reporter = MultiReporter(
            sub_reporters=[mock_reporter1, mock_reporter2],
            close_output_files=self.mock_close_output_files,
            output=self.mock_output
        )
        
        # Act
        reporter.linter(mock_linter)
        
        # Assert
        self.assertEqual(reporter._linter, mock_linter)
        # Check that linter was set on each mock reporter
        self.assertEqual(mock_reporter1.linter, mock_linter)
        self.assertEqual(mock_reporter2.linter, mock_linter)

    def test_linter_attribute_access(self):
        """Test that linter can be accessed as attribute after being set."""
        # Arrange
        mock_linter = Mock(spec=PyLinter)
        
        # Act
        self.reporter.linter(mock_linter)
        
        # Assert
        self.assertEqual(self.reporter._linter, mock_linter)

    @patch('pylint.reporters.multi_reporter.os.getcwd')
    def test_linter_with_custom_initialization(self, mock_getcwd):
        """Test linter method with custom initialization parameters."""
        # Arrange
        mock_getcwd.return_value = '/test/path'
        mock_linter = Mock(spec=PyLinter)
        
        # Create mock sub-reporters
        mock_sub_reporter1 = Mock()

            close_output_files=self.mock_close_output_files,

        )

        # Assert

        self.assertEqual(reporter._path_strip_prefix, '/test/path' + os.sep)
        self.assertIsNone(reporter.out)
        # Check that linter was set on sub-reporters
        self.assertEqual(mock_sub_reporter1.linter, mock_linter)
        self.assertEqual(mock_sub_reporter2.linter, mock_linter)

        """Common Diagram Handler initialization."""
        self.config = handler.config
        self.args = handler.args
        self.module_names: bool = False
        self._set_default_options()
        self.linker = linker
        self.classdiagram: ClassDiagram  # defined by subclasses
        # Only pre-calculate depths if user has requested a max_depth
        if handler.config.max_depth is not None:
            # Detect which of the args are leaf nodes
            leaf_nodes = self.get_leaf_nodes()

            # Emit a warning if any of the args are not leaf nodes
            diff = set(self.args).difference(set(leaf_nodes))
            if len(diff) > 0:
                warnings.warn(
                    "Detected nested names within the specified packages. "
                    f"The following packages: {sorted(diff)} will be ignored for "
                    f"depth calculations, using only: {sorted(leaf_nodes)} as the base for limiting "
                    "package depth.",
                    stacklevel=2,
                )

            self.args_depths = {module: module.count(".") for module in leaf_nodes}

def get_diadefs(self, project: Project, linker: Linker) -> list[ClassDiagram]:
        """Get the diagram's configuration data.

        :param project:The pyreverse project
        :type project: pyreverse.utils.Project
        :param linker: The linker
        :type linker: pyreverse.inspector.Linker(IdGeneratorMixIn, LocalsVisitor)

        :returns: The list of diagram definitions
        :rtype: list(:class:`pylint.pyreverse.diagrams.ClassDiagram`)
        """
        #  read and interpret diagram definitions (Diadefs)
        diagrams = []
        generator = ClassDiadefGenerator(linker, self)
        for klass in self.config.classes:
            diagrams.append(generator.class_diagram(project, klass))
        if not diagrams:
            diagrams = DefaultDiadefGenerator(linker, self).visit(project)
        for diagram in diagrams:
            diagram.extract_relationships()
        return diagrams

def __init__(self, linker: Linker, handler: DiadefsHandler) -> None:
        """Common Diagram Handler initialization."""
        self.config = handler.config
        self.args = handler.args
        self.module_names: bool = False
        self._set_default_options()
        self.linker = linker
        self.classdiagram: ClassDiagram  # defined by subclasses
        # Only pre-calculate depths if user has requested a max_depth
        if handler.config.max_depth is not None:
            # Detect which of the args are leaf nodes
            leaf_nodes = self.get_leaf_nodes()

            # Emit a warning if any of the args are not leaf nodes
            diff = set(self.args).difference(set(leaf_nodes))
            if len(diff) > 0:
                warnings.warn(
                    "Detected nested names within the specified packages. "
                    f"The following packages: {sorted(diff)} will be ignored for "
                    f"depth calculations, using only: {sorted(leaf_nodes)} as the base for limiting "
                    "package depth.",
                    stacklevel=2,
                )

            self.args_depths = {module: module.count(".") for module in leaf_nodes}

def class_diagram(self, project: Project, klass: nodes.ClassDef) -> ClassDiagram:
        """Return a class diagram definition for the class and related classes."""
        self.classdiagram = ClassDiagram(klass, self.config.mode)
        if len(project.modules) > 1:
            module, klass = klass.rsplit(".", 1)
            module = project.get_module(module)
        else:
            module = project.modules[0]
            klass = klass.split(".")[-1]
        klass = next(module.ilookup(klass))

        anc_level, association_level = self._get_levels()
        self.extract_classes(klass, anc_level, association_level)
        return self.classdiagram

def __init__(
        self,
        checker: BaseChecker,
        msgid: str,
        msg: str,
        description: str,
        symbol: str,
        scope: str,
        minversion: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
        maxversion: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
        old_names: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
        shared: bool = False,
        default_enabled: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        self.checker_name = checker.name
        self.check_msgid(msgid)
        self.msgid = msgid
        self.symbol = symbol
        self.msg = msg
        self.description = description
        self.scope = scope
        self.minversion = minversion
        self.maxversion = maxversion
        self.shared = shared
        self.default_enabled = default_enabled
        self.old_names: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        if old_names:
            for old_msgid, old_symbol in old_names:
                self.check_msgid(old_msgid)
                self.old_names.append(
                    (old_msgid, old_symbol),
                )

def __init__(
        self,
        checker: BaseChecker,
        msgid: str,
        msg: str,
        description: str,
        symbol: str,
        scope: str,
        minversion: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
        maxversion: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
        old_names: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
        shared: bool = False,
        default_enabled: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        self.checker_name = checker.name
        self.check_msgid(msgid)
        self.msgid = msgid
        self.symbol = symbol
        self.msg = msg
        self.description = description
        self.scope = scope
        self.minversion = minversion
        self.maxversion = maxversion
        self.shared = shared
        self.default_enabled = default_enabled
        self.old_names: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        if old_names:
            for old_msgid, old_symbol in old_names:
                self.check_msgid(old_msgid)
                self.old_names.append(
                    (old_msgid, old_symbol),
                )

def target_info_from_filename(filename: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    """Transforms /some/path/foo.png into ('/some/path', 'foo.png', 'png')."""
    basename = os.path.basename(filename)
    storedir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(filename))
    target = os.path.splitext(filename)[-1][1:]
    return storedir, basename, target

def generate(
        self, outputfile: str | None = None, mapfile: str | None = None
    ) -> str:
        """Generates a graph file.

        :param str outputfile: filename and path [defaults to graphname.png]
        :param str mapfile: filename and path

        :rtype: str
        :return: a path to the generated file
        :raises RuntimeError: if the executable for rendering was not found
        """
        # pylint: disable=duplicate-code
        graphviz_extensions = ("dot", "gv")
        name = self.graphname
        if outputfile is None:
            target = "png"
            pdot, dot_sourcepath = tempfile.mkstemp(".gv", name)
            ppng, outputfile = tempfile.mkstemp(".png", name)
            os.close(pdot)
            os.close(ppng)
        else:
            _, _, target = target_info_from_filename(outputfile)
            if not target:
                target = "png"
                outputfile = outputfile + "." + target
            if target not in graphviz_extensions:
                pdot, dot_sourcepath = tempfile.mkstemp(".gv", name)
                os.close(pdot)
            else:
                dot_sourcepath = outputfile
        with open(dot_sourcepath, "w", encoding="utf8") as file:
            file.write(self.source)
        if target not in graphviz_extensions:
            if shutil.which(self.renderer) is None:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"Cannot generate `{outputfile}` because '{self.renderer}' "
                    "executable not found. Install graphviz, or specify a `.gv` "
                    "outputfile to produce the DOT source code."
                )
            if mapfile:
                subprocess.run(
                    [
                        self.renderer,
                        "-Tcmapx",
                        "-o",
                        mapfile,
                        "-T",
                        target,
                        dot_sourcepath,
                        "-o",
                        outputfile,
                    ],
                    check=True,
                )
            else:
                subprocess.run(
                    [self.renderer, "-T", target, dot_sourcepath, "-o", outputfile],
                    check=True,
                )
            os.unlink(dot_sourcepath)
        return outputfile
